day.text: Blair: Finley's count matches my visit, so that's settled. Casey, you're the one throwing at me while your Hawk story only clears Alex. I'd rather throw at Casey than at someone whose visit is confirmed by a second player.
day.note: Casey is pushing a throw at me, and Finley and Alex are both making Drew-visit claims that can't both be checked. I'll confirm my visit to Finley and point the throw toward Casey, whose Hawk claim rests on one visit.

day.text: Finley: Blair's visit to me is confirmed, so I won't throw at Blair. Casey's Hawk visit only clears Alex, and Alex's Owl story still has no named Mouser. Let's look at who visited Drew before anyone calls caw.
day.note: Blair's visit to me is confirmed, so I shouldn't back a throw at Blair. I'll keep the table on Casey's unverifiable Hawk-on-Alex story without calling caw.
Last beat of the day. Everything I could usefully say is already on the table, so I'll stay quiet and let the vote run.

day.text: Alex: Blair's visit to Finley is confirmed by both of them, so I'm less worried there. Casey, your only clear story is that you visited me, and that's all it proves. I'm leaning toward throwing at Casey.
day.note: Casey's only support is a Hawk visit to me, and Blair's visit to Finley is confirmed by Finley, so I lean toward Casey as the throw. I won't call caw yet.

day.text: Finley's Falcon visit to Drew points at Blair. Drew was winked, which means a Mouser, and Blair is the one player whose visit only Blair confirms. Throw at Blair, calling caw.
day.note: Drew was winked, so a Mouser is in play, and Blair is the only player whose visit I can't check. Finley's Falcon visit to Drew points to Drew having visited someone, which leaves Blair as the likeliest Mouser. I'll push the throw and caw.

day.text: Ellis, Turkey, Farm. Blair's visit to Finley is confirmed by both of them, so I won't throw at Blair. Casey, your round 2 Owl story was wrong and your Hawk claim only clears Alex. I'm leaning toward Casey.
day.note: Casey is pushing a throw at Blair while Blair's visit is confirmed. Casey's round 2 Owl story was also wrong, so I'll lean toward Casey and not call caw yet.

Alex.note: I'm the Owl this round, Farm. Drew leads the scoreboard and I want to see who visited them.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia with a Mouser and a Wink, and I'm last on points. I'll visit Drew, the leader, to learn their role and find out who to protect or target.

Casey.note: As the Hawk with no fresh information, I'll visit Alex, who has pushed hardest against Farm players in recent rounds.

Drew.note: I'm Farm as the Kookaburra. Blair's claims have been inconsistent, so I'll visit Blair to learn their role.

Finley.note: I'm Meowfia as the Sphinx. Farm roles in play are Hawk, Kookaburra, Owl, Turkey. I'll visit the Hawk to learn who holds it.

lines: No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Animals that visited Drew: Mouser.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Drew is the Kookaburra.
You hold 1 Wink.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
You lost 2 eggs. You must discard 2.
Blair is the Kookaburra.
You were confused tonight: this report may be wrong.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
The Hawk is Casey.

Alex.feeling: Confusing and frustrating: the table keeps arguing over egg counts and fake visit stories, and Drew's death and Casey's caw leave the Mouser question unresolved.

Blair.feeling: Tense and cluttered: Casey is pushing a throw at me on thin evidence, and the Drew visit claims are hard to verify.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: the claims conflict, the table is pushing throws at me, and I'm trying to keep my own story clean.

Drew.feeling: Murky and tense: I'm already dead this round, so I can only watch the table argue over claims I can't verify.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: several claims contradict each other, Drew was winked, and I'm still unsure who the Mouser is.

Finley.feeling: Tense and a bit uncomfortable, since I'm Meowfia and have to build a believable Farm story while the table pushes on Casey and Blair.

Alex.note: Casey's Owl story was false last round and Casey is pushing to throw at Blair, whose visit Finley confirmed. I'll throw two low cards at Casey.

Blair.note: Alex, Ellis, and Finley are leaning toward Casey, so I'll join the throw at Casey with a single low card to keep my high cards.

Casey.note: Blair is my best Mouser suspect, and I have no better target. I'll throw my two low cards at Blair and keep my 12s.

Drew.note: I'm dead, so my throw won't count as a vote, but it still scores. Casey's Owl story in round 2 was wrong and Casey is pushing a throw at Blair, so I'll throw one low card at Casey.

Ellis.note: I'm only moderately confident about Casey, so I'll throw one Wild. It keeps the vote but risks only one point of value.

Finley.note: Casey is Farm, and eggsecuting a Farm player is a Meowfia win. Alex and Ellis are both leaning toward Casey, so I'll throw there with two low cards.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Eagle reports were hard to check: it wasn't clear whether a visitor to a player's nest counted as a visit to my target, and I misread my own Eagle gain as coming from my target's visitors.
Alex.fun: Winking Ellis mid-day in round 1 was tense, and watching the table react to Ellis going silent was the most engaging moment.
Alex.change: Make the dawn reports state exactly who visited whom, so players can check each claim against nest counts instead of arguing over ambiguous egg changes.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I winked Ellis, a Farm player, which exposed my Mouser play and didn't help my side. Instead I would have kept my wink and stayed quieter until the vote.

Blair.confusing: The night-egg rules for Owl and Eagle were hard to track, since the "visited no one" and visitor-count wording made it unclear when an egg was actually laid. Alex and Casey's Round 2 accounts only made sense once I worked it out.
Blair.fun: Getting the Falcon visit on Alex in Round 2 and watching Alex's Eagle +1 line up with it, which exposed Casey's false Owl story, was satisfying.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports name the visitor count and egg source more explicitly, so players can check claims without reconstructing every night.
Blair.regret: In Round 2 I joined the throw at Casey and called caw while Drew, the Floofer Meowfia, went unchallenged; I should have pressed Drew's visit story instead of defending Alex's Eagle count.

Casey.confusing: Whether a Falcon or Owl visit counts toward a target's egg change was unclear, and several players argued about it wrongly. Also, a Mouser's Wink was never explained at the table, so Drew's death could not be checked.
Casey.fun: Round 1: my Hawk visit to Blair gained an egg, and Farm voted Blair out, which was correct. Watching the claims contradict each other across the table was the most enjoyable part.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports state the source of every egg change, so players can check claims like Eagle and Owl counts directly.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw three cards at Alex, a Farm player, and lost them when Farm lost; I should have kept my high cards and thrown only the Wild and one low card. I would also have voted for Blair in round 3 with fewer cards, since Farm lost anyway.

Drew.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track, since a confused player's report can be wrong and nobody could tell which claims were confused. Round 2's Owl and Eagle egg counts were also hard to reconcile.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was fun to play as Meowfia: the table locked onto Casey, and our team won by eggsecuting a Farm player who had been deflecting well.
Drew.change: I would make egg counts and visit claims easier to verify, perhaps by having the Storyteller publish each player's exact egg change at dawn.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I should have pushed harder on Blair, whose visit claim was never verified. Blair and Finley were both Meowfia, so I would have thrown at Blair and kept my high cards instead of trusting the table's Casey push.

Ellis.confusing: How the night visits and egg counts were reported, since a Kookaburra visit confuses the visitor and the Owl/Eagle counts were hard to cross-check. Several players' stories only made sense once the hidden roles were revealed.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went well: the Kookaburra read on Casey, combined with the table, got Blair eggsecuted and banked my 12.
Ellis.change: Show each player's visit and egg change in a shared log so the table can check claims without relying on memory.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I backed the throw at Casey, a Farm Owl, on Alex's Eagle read, when Drew was the Floofer hiding as Meowfia. I would have pushed for a clearer count from Drew before joining the throw.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were hard to read, since an Owl only lays an egg when nobody else visited, so several true claims looked false. Being confused also made my own Kookaburra report unreliable.
Finley.fun: Playing the Sphinx in round 3 was fun: I steered the day quietly while posing as a Falcon, and the table threw at a Farm player, which handed Meowfia the round.
Finley.change: I'd make dawn reports say clearly when a player was confused and which parts might be wrong, so nobody has to guess.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I helped throw at Casey on thin evidence without first pressing Alex to explain the egg gain, so I'd hold the throw until the counts add up.

review.title: Winks and Wrong Owls
review.headline: Farm caught the cat in round one, then ate its own Owl twice.
review.summary: Round 1 went to Farm: Casey's Hawk hit on Blair was real, and Alex's Wink on Ellis could not save the cats. Rounds 2 and 3 went the other way. The table piled onto Casey, a Farm Owl, because the egg-count logic was muddled, and Meowfia won both. Casey and Ellis tied at 18, but the tiebreak is not in the rules. Casey was the only player to correctly guess a cat in round 1, then was wrongly eggsecuted twice.

rounds.recap: Casey's Hawk hit on Blair gave Farm a real lead. Alex, a Mouser, claimed a fake Hawk and winked Ellis, which did not help. Blair also claimed a visit to Ellis that Ellis's lack of confusion disproved. Four players threw at Blair, who was Meowfia, and Farm won.

Drew, the only Meowfia, hugged Casey, so Casey's Owl result was blank. Alex's Eagle claim named Drew as Casey's visitor, which was true. Nobody could square the egg counts. Casey's Owl story looked false, five players threw at Casey, and Meowfia Drew won with only one thrown card.

Blair, a Mouser, winked Drew, the Kookaburra, on day one. Alex's true Owl report about a Mouser led nowhere because the Owl sees animals, not players. Finley lied that she was a Falcon, and Casey's accusation of Blair was dismissed because of her bad round-2 record. Casey was eggsecuted again and the two cats won.

highlights.text: Alex winked Ellis mid-argument. It silenced Ellis, but Ellis still threw D12 from beyond the grave and banked 12.
Ellis argued that a Kookaburra visited would be confused, so Blair's and Alex's claimed visits must be false. This was a clean deduction from the rules.
Drew was the lone Meowfia and survived by agreeing with the crowd. He threw one S9 and won 9 points while five Farm players threw away their cards.
Blair winked Drew before anyone spoke. Drew could have exposed the Mouser, and the wink removed that threat.

confusions.what: Claimed to have visited Ellis, a Kookaburra. Ellis was not confused, so the visit could not have happened.
Claimed Hawk and expected a visit to Ellis to show nothing, ignoring that a visit would confuse Ellis.
Opened by saying her seat was gone and that she was a replacement, then had to correct herself.
Said Casey's Owl visit would have added an egg to his nest. He was a visited target with other visitors, so the Owl rule did not apply.
Said her Falcon visit explained Alex's +1. Falcons lay no eggs, and Alex's Eagle count came from visitors to Casey.
Said nobody visited her, though Drew and Alex did. Hugged Owls and Eagle logic confused her.
Said Alex's Eagle egg comes from visitors to Alex. It comes from visitors to the Eagle's target.
Used Casey's unchanged nest as proof that she was lying. A hugged Owl would also show no change.
Overlooked that the Owl's report was a general Mouser clue the Meowfia could ignore. The table also kept asking him to name the Mouser.
Treated a confirmed visit as proof Blair was clean, but a Meowfia can match a visit story with a cat teammate.

worked: Kookaburra confusion created a real rules-based deduction in round 1: Ellis's non-confusion exposed two false visit claims.
The Wink created tension in both rounds it was used. A Mouser can silence an accuser or the Kookaburra before they speak.
Throw counts are public and values are secret. The consolation returned a high card to Alex and Blair in round 1.
problems: Night logic is hard to verify. Owl, Eagle, Falcon and Floofer effects interact (hugs, confusion, empty visits), and players misapplied them repeatedly. Add a short per-animal cheat sheet, or a worked example.
The Floofer's hug on a Farm Owl produced misleading blank results. Casey was eggsecuted twice for honest play. Consider letting a hugged player learn they were hugged.
The Owl reports animals only, which was a dead end in round 3. Alex's true clue about a Mouser could not be acted on. Give the Owl one more detail or a clearer use.
Scores snowball. After round 1 Casey and Ellis led, and Alex was far behind, so Alex had no way back to first. Add a catch-up mechanism or reduce banking value.
The rules do not say how ties for first are resolved. Casey and Ellis both finished with 18.
